chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Throw [the pebbles] each day at the decline of the sun, and say [the supplication], and he mentioned the supplication. Therefore, the meaning in this report is that we should interpret it as recommended virtue and preference, rather than obligatory duty and compulsion.

key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: Recommendation / Preferability (a category of fiqh ruling)
key_terms.زَوَالِ الشَّمْسِ: Decline of the sun (time for Dhuhr prayer)

ai.seo_question: Is throwing pebbles at the Jamarat at a specific time obligatory or recommended in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifies the time for stoning the Jamarat as the decline of the sun (Zawal), while clarifying that this timing is recommended (mustahabb) rather than strictly obligatory (wajib). This distinction highlights the flexibility in Hajj rituals, allowing pilgrims to perform the act within this preferred window without incurring sin if delayed, reflecting the Shia juristic approach to balancing ritual precision with ease for the worshippers.
